CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steven W. Huang, DDS, Mayor  www.SanMarinoCA.gov
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Tony Chou, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

Calvin Lo, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Steve Talt, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 09, 2024 AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626)
300-0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov until 3:00
  p.m. the day before the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will

AGENDA – OCTOBER 09, 2024  PAGE 1 of 6
   be distributed to City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00
  p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not provided to City Council
  at the meeting.
  Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us
  teleconference module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted
  after the in-person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Talt, Vice Mayor Shepherd
Romey, and Mayor Huang

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.SanMarinoCA.gov.
PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to
place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.
CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

  PRESENTATION

 CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION FOR EAGLE SCOUT HOWARD CHEN

 CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION FOR DR. HWEI-CHIH CHENG SUN AND
 PRESENTATION AND DONATION OF THE MEMOIRS OF DR. HWEI-CHIH
 CHENG SUN BY DR. RICHARD SUN, DR. CHRISTINA SUN, AND DR.
 GEORGE SUN TO THE CITY OF SAN MARINO’S CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY
 AND A $20,000 DONATION TO THE SAN MARINO PUBLIC LIBRARY
 FOUNDATION

AGENDA – OCTOBER 09, 2024  PAGE 2 of 6
   PUBLIC HEARINGS

 1.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL FOR A MILLS ACT PROGRAM FOR THE
  PROPERTY LOCATED AT 708 WINSTON AVENUE

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution R-24-27.
  If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R-24-27, approving the Mills Act Contract for the
  property located at 708 Winston Avenue that is attached to the Staff report.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

 2.  AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO ENTER INTO A METRO-APPROVED
  AGREEMENT WITH THE CITY OF PASADENA TO EXCHANGE $1,000,000
  OF THE CITY'S PROPOSITION A LOCAL RETURN FUNDS FOR $750,000
  OF CITY OF PASADENA'S GENERAL FUND DOLLARS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council authorize the City to enter into a
  Metro-Approved agreement with the City of Pasadena to exchange $1,000,000 of the
  City’s Proposition A Local Return Funds for $750,000 of the City of Pasadena’s
  General Fund dollars. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to authorize the City to enter into a Metro-Approved agreement with the City
  of Pasadena to exchange $1,000,000 of the City’s Proposition A Local Return Funds
  for $750,000 of the City of Pasadena’s General Fund dollars and authorize the City
  Manager or his designee to take such further actions necessary to effectuate the
  agreement.”

 3.  FIND THE ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATIONS PROJECT EXEMPT
  UNDER THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA);
  AWARD A CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT TO ABM ELECTRICAL &
  LIGHTING SOLUTIONS FOR ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATIONS
  PROJECT NO. 24-1009 IN THE LOW BID AMOUNT OF $57,129.00, AND
  REJECT ALL OTHER BIDS; AND AUTHORIZE THE PARKS AND PUBLIC
  WORKS DIRECTOR/CITY ENGINEER TO APPROVE CONSTRUCTION
  CONTINGENCIES IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $10,000.00

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council 1.) find the project
  categorically exempt under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to Section 15301 of Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations (Class 1,
  Existing Facilities exemption), 2.) award a Construction Agreement to ABM Electrical
  & Lighting Solutions, 3.) authorize the Parks and Public Works Director/City Engineer

AGENDA – OCTOBER 09, 2024  PAGE 3 of 6
   to approve contract change orders and other contingencies in an amount not to
  exceed $11,425.80. If the Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to 1.) find the Electric Vehicle Charger Installation Project exempt from
  review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section
  15301 of Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations (Class 1, Existing
  Facilities exemption), 2.) award a Construction Agreement to ABM Electrical &
  Lighting Solutions, for the Electric Vehicle Charging Station Project No. 24-1009 in
  the amount of $57,129.00, and reject all other bids, and 3.) authorize the Parks and
  Public Works Director/City Engineer to approve contract change orders and other
  contingencies in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00.”

 4.  APPROVAL OF CONTRACT RENEWAL WITH HINDERLITER, DE LLAMAS
  AND ASSOCIATES TO PROVIDE BUSINESS LICENSE SOFTWARE
  SERVICES THROUGH NOVEMBER 11, 2027

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the contract and authorize
  the City Manager to execute the agreement. If Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the contract renewal with HdL, which will extend the agreement
  for a term to expire on November 11, 2027, for their continued business license
  software services, and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.”

 5.  APPROVAL FOR THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE A SPECIAL EVENT
  PERMIT AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN MARINO MOTOR CLASSIC

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council authorize the City Manager to
  execute an agreement with the San Marino Motor Classic through December 31,
  2029.

  If the City Council deems the agreement satisfactory, an appropriate motion would
  be:
  “I move to authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with the San Marino
  Motor Classic through December 31, 2029.”

 6.  CALIFORNIA OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES DESIGNATION OF
  APPLICANT’S AGENT RESOLUTION FOR NON-STATE AGENCIES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council authorize the completion and filing
  of the Designation of Applicant’s Agent Resolution for Non-State Agencies. If the City
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  "I move that the City Council approve the completion and filing of the Designation of
  Applicant’s Agent Resolution for Non-State Agencies designating the City Manager,
  Finance Director, and Fire Chief as authorized agents for the City of San Marino.”

 7.  CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF AUGUST 2024

AGENDA – OCTOBER 09, 2024  PAGE 4 of 6
   Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of August
  2024.”

 8.  RECEIVE AND FILE  MONTHLY  DISBURSEMENTS  REPORT  FOR
  SEPTEMBER 2024

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of September 2024. If the City Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of
  September 2024.”

 9.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the September 2024
  minutes. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to approve the minutes of the regular meeting of September 11, 2024, and
  the adjourned regular meeting of September 27, 2024.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
